es.summary: Fenómeno en el que el fármaco administrado por vía oral es metabolizado en el hígado antes de alcanzar la circulación sistémica, reduciendo su biodisponibilidad.
key_points: Reduce la fracción de fármaco activo que llega a la sangre.
Varía según la vía de administración y la función hepática.
Influye en la dosificación y la eficacia clínica.
Puede ser evitado con formulaciones sublinguales o parenterales.

mechanism: El fármaco absorbido del tracto gastrointestinal pasa al hígado a través de la vena porta.
Enzimáticamente, el hígado transforma parte del fármaco en metabolitos inactivos.
Solo la fracción no metabolizada entra a la circulación sistémica (bioavailability).
Factores como edad, enfermedad hepática y consumo de alcohol modifican la magnitud del efecto.
nursing_care: Evaluar función hepática (AST, ALT, bilirrubina) antes de iniciar fármacos con alto efecto de primer paso.
Monitorear niveles plasmáticos del fármaco cuando estén disponibles.
Ajustar la dosis si la prueba de función hepática está alterada.
Retener la medicación y notificar al médico si aparecen signos de toxicidad hepática.
Preferir vías alternativas (sublingual, transdérmica) si el paciente tiene insuficiencia hepática.
patient_teaching: Explicar que la absorción oral puede ser menor por el efecto de primer paso.
Indicar la importancia de no omitir dosis y de seguir la vía de administración prescrita.
Advertir sobre el consumo de alcohol o alimentos grasos que pueden alterar la metabolización.
Informar que algunos medicamentos pueden requerir toma con alimentos para reducir el efecto de primer paso.

outcomes: Nivel terapéutico del fármaco dentro del rango esperado
Seguridad del paciente sin signos de toxicidad

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar pruebas de función hepática antes de iniciar la terapia.
interventions.rationale: Detectar alteraciones que puedan aumentar la exposición al fármaco.

interventions.action: Monitorear niveles séricos del fármaco cuando estén indicados.
interventions.rationale: Asegurar que la concentración permanezca dentro del rango terapéutico.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de la vía de administración prescrita y evitar automedicación.
interventions.rationale: Reducir la variabilidad en la absorción y metabolismo del fármaco.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de toxicidad (náuseas, ictericia, alteración del estado mental) cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Detectar precozmente una posible sobredosis o acumulación.

interventions.action: Comunicar al médico cualquier alteración en pruebas hepáticas o aparición de efectos adversos.
interventions.rationale: Permitir ajuste de dosis o cambio de vía de administración.

en.summary: Phenomenon in which an orally administered drug is metabolized in the liver before reaching systemic circulation, reducing its bioavailability.
key_points: Reduces the fraction of active drug that reaches the bloodstream.
Varies according to route of administration and liver function.
Can be avoided with sublingual or parenteral formulations.

mechanism: The drug absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract passes to the liver via the portal vein.
Enzymatically, the liver converts part of the drug into inactive metabolites.
Only the unmetabolized fraction enters systemic circulation (bioavailability).
Factors such as age, liver disease, and alcohol consumption modify the magnitude of the effect.
nursing_care: Assess liver function (AST, ALT, bilirubin) before starting drugs with high first-pass effect.
Monitor plasma drug levels when available.
Adjust the dose if liver function tests are altered.
Hold medication and notify the physician if signs of hepatic toxicity appear.
Prefer alternative routes (sublingual, transdermal) if the patient has liver insufficiency.
patient_teaching: Explain that oral absorption may be lower due to the first-pass effect.
Emphasize the importance of not skipping doses and following the prescribed route of administration.
Warn about alcohol or high-fat foods that can alter metabolism.
Inform that some medications may need to be taken with food to reduce the first-pass effect.

outcomes: Therapeutic drug level within expected range
Patient safety without signs of toxicity

interventions.action: Obtain and record liver function tests before initiating therapy.
interventions.rationale: Detect alterations that may increase drug exposure.

interventions.action: Monitor serum drug levels when indicated.
interventions.rationale: Ensure concentration remains within therapeutic range.

interventions.action: Educate the patient on the importance of the prescribed route of administration and avoid self-medication.
interventions.rationale: Reduce variability in absorption and drug metabolism.

interventions.action: Assess for signs of toxicity (nausea, jaundice, altered mental status) each shift.
interventions.rationale: Detect early a possible overdose or accumulation.

interventions.action: Communicate to the physician any changes in liver tests or appearance of adverse effects.
interventions.rationale: Allow dose adjustment or change of route of administration.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics

summary.0.quote: After absorption, oral drugs can also be metabolized in the liver before entering systemic circulation, a process called first-pass metabolism.

key_points.0.quote: This can decrease the bioavailability of a drug.

sections.mechanism.0.quote: The medication is absorbed by the intestinal mucosa, and it travels across the membranes into the portal vein.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: During the first pass through the liver via the portal circulation, the drug is metabolized into active and inactive metabolites.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Price and Patel (2022) define bioavailability “for majority purposes” as “the fraction of the active form of a drug that reaches system circulation unaltered.”

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Monitoring liver enzymes and drug-level concentrations will help ensure that drug concentrations remain therapeutic (Herman & Santos, 2023).

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Drug concentrations can also accumulate if drug-metabolizing organs are not functioning properly and the dose is not adjusted accordingly.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: After absorption, oral drugs can also be metabolized in the liver before entering systemic circulation, a process called first-pass metabolism.
